segments.say: Is this move even legal? Most beginners say no.
segments.caption: Legal or illegal?

segments.say: White pushes the pawn. Black brings out the knight.
segments.caption: Normal start

segments.say: White pushes again, attacking the knight. Black plays d5, right next to the white pawn.
segments.caption: Pawn jumps next to it

segments.say: Now the white pawn captures diagonally, onto an empty square. And the black pawn disappears.
segments.caption: Wait... what?!

segments.say: Yes, it's legal. It's called en passant. If a pawn jumps two squares to land next to yours, you can capture it like it only moved one. But only on the very next move.
segments.caption: 100% legal

segments.say: Did you know this rule? Comment yes or no, and follow for more.
segments.caption: Did you know this rule?
